retained.name: surface_contact_entropy
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss is governed by the fraction of adsorbate surface in contact with pore walls: molecules whose Labute ASA is large relative to the local pore dimension product (lsd_f * lsd_p) experience stronger adsorbent-surface vibrational locking, and frame density (source scale) modulates wall interaction strength; this contact-descriptor should reduce MAE of entropy loss/R in the strong-adsorption (micropore) regime.

retained.name: inertial_mass_entropy
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss depends on the ratio of molecular mass to its largest moment of inertia: heavy compact molecules (large MW/PMI3) convert gas-phase rotation into hindered librations almost completely upon adsorption, so an exponential decay in MW/PMI3, gated by the accessible-volume-to-frame-cell ratio Vol/lsd_f**3, should reduce MAE of entropy loss/R in the strongly bound regime where the retained contact descriptor underperforms.

retained.name: packing_fraction_vibrational_gate
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss/R decreases with the log of accessible framework volume per unit adsorbate mass (Vol/MW), a specific-pore-volume-like quantity, and this translational-degrees-of-freedom effect is gated by the ratio of accessible volume AV to the wall-area scale lsd_f*LabuteASA: light molecules in large-pore frameworks retain near-gas entropy, while the same molecule in a high-AV/area-gate framework loses less entropy than a low-gate framework; the product should reduce MAE of entropy loss/R in the weak-to-intermediate adsorption regime, complementary to the retained strongly bound regime descriptors.

retained.name: aperture_mismatch_freedom_index
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss is governed by the mismatch between framework limiting pore size (lsd_f) and probe-accessible pore size (lsd_p), modulated by molecular smallest dimension PBF; when |lsd_f - lsd_p| is large relative to the molecular cross-section PBF, the adsorbate sits in a loose, cavity-like environment with small entropy loss, whereas near-zero mismatch forces tight packing with large entropy loss. This descriptor will reduce MAE of entropy loss/R relative to a model using AV alone, falsified if the MAE does not improve or if the fitted relationship is not the predicted non-monotonic (minimum near mismatch ~ PBF) form.

retained.name: free_volume_per_contact_area_index
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss/R decreases with the free-volume-per-molecular-surface ratio: frameworks offering more accessible volume per unit of molecular contact surface allow the adsorbate to retain more positional freedom, while low AV relative to molecular surface area forces wall contact and larger entropy loss. This descriptor will improve MAE of entropy loss/R below 0.5416 relative to the retained aperture_mismatch_freedom_index.

retained.name: occ_volume_confinement_ratio
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss (s_gas - s_ads)/R correlates with the ratio of framework accessible volume per gram to molecular van der Waals volume; tighter ratio means stronger confinement and larger entropy loss. Adding this nonlinear re-expression on top of the full 14-input network lowers MAE of entropy loss/R versus the baseline network.

retained.name: gravimetric_surface_confinement
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss/R grows with the ratio of framework-specific surface area per pore volume (ASA/AV, wall-contact availability) relative to the molecule's own surface-per-volume density (LabuteASA/Vol): frameworks offering many wall sites per unit pore space relative to the guest's contact density immobilize guests more strongly, so adding this material-vs-molecule surface coupling lowers MAE of entropy loss/R below the round-1 retained baseline (0.5431).
